description:
Orbital Delulu is a team of six first-year B.Tech students ready to turn curiosity into creation. United by our interest in technology, innovation, and space, we're taking on the NASA Space Apps Challenge to learn, experiment, and build something beyond the ordinary. 

Six beginners. One mission. Ideas in orbit. 🚀

We may be delulu, but our ideas are definitely in orbit. 🚀
summary:
Mission Architect: Mars Odyssey is an interactive, open-world space exploration and Mars mission simulation game. It allows players to explore space environments, select spacecraft, plan missions, perform launch and orbital operations, inspect satellites, operate Mars rovers, and experience the journey from Earth to Mars.

Our project addresses the challenge of making complex space science and aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand through interactive gameplay rather than theory alone. Players learn about spacecraft operations, mission planning, and planetary exploration while completing objectives in a connected space environment.

Unlike traditional level-based games, our platform focuses on open-world exploration and expandable missions. Our vision is to inspire students and space enthusiasts to explore, learn, and develop an interest in future space technologies.
details:
Mission Architect: Mars Odyssey is an interactive, open-world space exploration and Mars mission simulation game designed to make space science and aerospace engineering more engaging and accessible.

How Does It Work?

The game allows players to explore different space environments, select spacecraft, prepare missions, and experience various stages of space exploration. Players can perform launch operations, explore Earth and Mars orbits, inspect satellites, operate Mars rovers, and work towards establishing a Mars base. A mission progression system tracks achievements and completed objectives, while tutorials help beginners understand the controls and gameplay.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our project transforms complex space-related concepts into an interactive learning experience. It helps players develop curiosity about space science, understand basic aerospace engineering concepts, and explore the challenges of interplanetary missions. Our intended impact is to encourage students and space enthusiasts to learn through exploration, experimentation, and problem-solving.

Tools and Technologies Used

We developed the project as a web-based game using:

  • HTML5: Game structure and interface.
  • CSS3: Styling, layouts, and visual design.
  • JavaScript: Game mechanics, interactions, mission progression, and functionality.
  • Visual Studio Code: Development environment.
  • AI-assisted development tools: Supporting code generation, debugging, and development.

What Makes It Creative?

Our main innovation is combining open-world exploration with mission-based gameplay and educational elements. Instead of presenting isolated missions, we aim to create one connected universe where players can travel between environments and experience space exploration as a continuous journey. The modular design also allows future missions, spacecraft, and locations to be added.

Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific relevance and educational value.
  • Beginner-friendly controls and tutorials.
  • Engaging gameplay and realistic space environments.
  • Mission progression and player achievements.
  • Performance and browser compatibility.
  • Expandability for future space exploration missions.

Our ultimate goal is to make space exploration more interactive, educational, and inspiring while encouraging the next generation to think beyond Earth.
